description: One block, restricted from entry until one moment, because of one product. A tank mix that went out over four blocks writes four of these — the window is a fact about a PLACE and the label that reached it, not about the machine that drove there, and a worker asking 'may I walk into this row' is asking about the row. Created by record_spray_application; closed by close_expired_reis or by the next read that finds it expired. Nothing about a person's entry is stored here: this record says the block is restricted, not who went in.

fields.description: Active until the window passes, then Expired. Cancelled is a window somebody withdrew — a spray that was logged against the wrong block — and is kept rather than deleted, because a restriction that was published to a crew and then lifted is itself a thing an inspector may ask about.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: Which register the restricted block is in — 'Field' for a planted block, 'Asset Register' for a block-shaped asset tag. A DYNAMIC LINK because this app has both and a spray reaches whichever one the farm actually maps its rows in; the same pair Farm Task uses for location_doctype/location, so a task raised on a block and a restriction on the same block key alike.
fields.label: Block DocType

fields.description: The block this restriction is on.
fields.label: Block

fields.description: The machine that applied it. Recorded because a scan of the sprayer should tell whoever is holding it what it left behind, and because a mis-set rate is traced through the machine. It is NOT what the window belongs to — see the doctype description.
fields.label: Sprayer

fields.description: The Farm Task this spray closed, where it came off one. A spray logged at the machine with no task raised for it has this empty, and that is a legitimate record rather than a gap — the restriction is real either way.
fields.label: Source Task

fields.description: The item whose label set this window — THE LONGEST REI IN THE TANK, not the first product and not an average. A mix of a four-hour and a twenty-four-hour product restricts the block for twenty-four hours, and the block does not become half-enterable at hour twelve. Every other product in the mix is listed in All Products.
fields.label: Product (Longest REI)

fields.description: The product's name as the register spells it, copied at application time. Stored rather than fetched so a warning read years later still names what actually went out, even if the Item has since been renamed or disabled.
fields.label: Product Name

fields.description: Hours of restricted entry, off the product's own rei_hours column.
fields.label: REI Hours

fields.description: Every product in the tank as JSON — [{item_code, item_name, qty, uom, rei_hours}] — because the one that set the window is not the whole of what a worker was exposed to, and a medical question asked after the fact is asked about the mix.
fields.label: All Products

fields.description: When the application finished. The window runs from here and not from when this record was written, so a spray filed off a handset that was out of signal for two hours does not restrict the block for two hours longer than the label says.
fields.label: Started At

fields.description: When entry is permitted again — started_at plus rei_hours, computed once and STORED rather than derived on every read. A stored instant is what a worker was told at the tailgate, and it stays true if somebody later corrects the interval on the Item.
fields.label: Expires At

fields.description: When this record was moved off Active. For an expiry that is the moment the sweep or a read noticed, which is at or after expires_at — the two are kept apart because the difference is the lag in the closing, and expires_at is the compliance fact.
fields.label: Closed At

fields.description: Set when the scheduled sweep closed this rather than a person.
fields.label: Closed By Scheduled Job

name: Spray REI
